{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash
# NOTE: The SLURM '--no-requeue' option is not directly translatable to Flux.
# Job requeue behavior in Flux is typically configured at the system level.

# set the job name
#FLUX --job-name="sgemm_thin"

# NOTE: The SLURM '--get-user-env' directive is generally the default behavior for
# schedulers and does not require an explicit option in Flux.

#FLUX --chdir=/u/dssc/mdepet00/assignment/exercise2
#FLUX --queue=THIN
#FLUX --nodes=1
#FLUX --exclusive
#FLUX --ntasks-per-node=1
#FLUX --cpus-per-task=12
#FLUX --mem=490G
#FLUX --time=02:00:00
#FLUX --output=sgemm_thin_job_{id}.out

#module load architecture/AMD
#module load openMPI/4.1.4/gnu/12.2.1
module load mkl
#module load openBLAS/0.3.21-omp
module load openBLAS/0.3.23-omp

#mpirun -np 1 make all

export OMP_PLACES=cores
export OMP_PROC_BIND=spread
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=12
export BLIS_NUM_THREADS=12
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/u/dssc/mdepet00/assignment/exercise2/blis/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH

echo size scalability begin

now=$(date +"%Y-%m-%d_%H-%M-%S")
for LIB in oblas_optimized oblas mkl_optimized mkl blis_optimized blis; do
  csvname=sgemm_"$LIB"_thin_$(hostname)_$now.csv
  #echo "$csvname $(hostname) $now"
  #echo "$csvname"
  #2000,2000,2000,0.034462963,0.034463,464.266523
  echo "m,n,k,elapsed1,elapsed2,GFLOPS" >"$csvname"
done
for REP in {1..10}; do
  for LIB in oblas_optimized oblas mkl_optimized mkl blis_optimized blis; do
  csvname=sgemm_"$LIB"_thin_$(hostname)_$now.csv
  # 'srun' is replaced by 'flux run'. The resource options from srun are now
  # defined at the job level.
  #flux run -n1 ./sgemm_oblas.x 2000 2000 200>discarded_first_result_"$csvname"
  #echo "$csvname $(hostname) $now">"$csvname"
    #increase the size of matrices size from 2000x2000 to 20000x20000 (single precision) and analyse the scaling of the GEMM calculation for at least MKL and openblas.
    for SIZE in {30000..2000..500}; do
      # The SLURM_JOB_ID variable is replaced with the Flux equivalent, FLUX_JOB_ID
      echo sgemm_thin_job_"$FLUX_JOB_ID".out$'\t'"$csvname"$'\t'"$(hostname)"$'\t'rep "$REP" size "$SIZE" OMP_PLACES=$OMP_PLACES OMP_PROC_BIND=$OMP_PROC_BIND OMP_NUM_THREADS=$OMP_NUM_THREADS BLIS_NUM_THREADS=$BLIS_NUM_THREADS flux run -n1 ./sgemm_$LIB.x "$SIZE" "$SIZE" "$SIZE"'>>'"$csvname"
      flux run -n1 ./sgemm_$LIB.x "$SIZE" "$SIZE" "$SIZE" >>"$csvname"
      #flux run -n1 ./sgemm_oblas.x 2000 2000 2000
    done
  done
done

now=$(date +"%Y-%m-%d_%H-%M-%S")
echo "$(hostname)" "$now" END
echo size scalability end
"

issues: There is a logging error in the script's main loop. The `echo` command is appending a long, descriptive string of the command being run directly into the CSV data file (`... >>"$csvname"`). This will corrupt the CSV file on every iteration by mixing metadata/log lines with the comma-separated data output from the `sgemm` executable, making the output difficult or impossible to parse. This logging information was likely intended to go to the job's standard output, not be redirected into the data file.
